record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: Do bi-integrable systems exist for each algebraic type? This question is local in the sense that bi-integrable systems in quest ion "live" in a small neighbourhood of a generic point x ∈ M where the algebraic type of a given Poisson pencil is locally constant. However, for applications, we need smooth commuting functions that are glob ally defined on the whole manifold M. For two constant brackets {, }1 and {, }2 on a vector space V, bi-integrable systems can be easily constructed by means of bi-Poisson linear algebra: each bi-Lagran gian subspace can be interpreted as a bi-integrable Hamiltonian system with linear integrals. The first non- trivial example is the so-called "argument shift" pencil (see A.S. Mischenko and A.T. Fomenko [172]), generated by a linear and a constant brackets. We recall this construction. 25 5.2 Argument shift method and Jordan-Kronecker invariants of Lie alge- bras Let g∗ be the dual space of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra g. It is well known that g∗ possesses two natural compatible Poisson brackets. The first one is the standar d linear Lie-Poisson bracket {f, g}(x) = <x, [d f(x), dg(x)]>, (5.3) and the second one is a constant bracket given by {f, g}a(x) = <a, [d f(x), dg(x)]>, (5.4) where a ∈ g∗ is a fixed element. Here we assume a to be regular, although formula (5.4) makes sense for an arbitrary a. There are many examples of finite-dimensional Lie algebras for which we can construct a complete family of polynomials in bi-involution with respect to the brackets (5.3) and (5.4). In particular, the famous theorem by A.S. Mischenko and A.T. Fomenko [172] states th at such a family exists for every semisimple Lie algebra g and consists of shifts of Ad ∗ -invariant polynomials, i.e., function of the form fi(x + λa), where λ ∈ R and f1,..., fr are generators of the algebra of (co)-adjoint invariants. However, it is still an open question whether one can construct suc h a family for every finite-dimensional Lie algebra. In many examples (see [38]), the answer turns out to be positive, leading us to the following Generalised Argument Shift conjecture which was first stated in [38 ] and then mentioned and discussed in a number of papers [195, 36, 122, 34]:

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $M$ be a smooth manifold equipped with two compatible Poisson structures $\{\,,\,\}_1$ and $\{\,,\,\}_2$ (i.e., every linear combination $\lambda_1\{\,,\,\}_1+\lambda_2\{\,,\,\}_2$ is again a Poisson bracket). The family $\mathcal{P}=\{\lambda_1\{\,,\,\}_1+\lambda_2\{\,,\,\}_2:(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2\setminus\{0\}\}$ is called a Poisson pencil on $M$.

For a generic point $x\in M$, the pair of skew-symmetric forms induced on $T_x^*M$ by the two brackets admits a Jordan–Kronecker canonical form, i.e., a decomposition into Jordan blocks (with eigenvalues $\lambda\in\overline{\mathbb{R}}$) and Kronecker blocks (of various odd sizes). The collection of these blocks (sizes and eigenvalues) is called the algebraic type of the pencil at $x$. On an open dense subset of $M$ the algebraic type is locally constant; this common type is the (generic) algebraic type of $\mathcal{P}$.

A bi-integrable system on $(M,\{\,,\,\}_1,\{\,,\,\}_2)$ is a family $\mathcal{F}$ of smooth functions on $M$, globally defined, that is:
(i) in bi-involution: $\{f,g\}_1=\{f,g\}_2=0$ for all $f,g\in\mathcal{F}$; and
(ii) complete in the sense that at a generic point the differentials of functions in $\mathcal{F}$ span a subspace of $T_x^*M$ which is bi-Lagrangian for the pair of forms, i.e., of maximal possible dimension compatible with bi-involution dictated by the algebraic type.

Problem. Determine whether, for every algebraic type of a Poisson pencil that can occur at a generic point, there exists a smooth manifold $M$ with a compatible pair $(\{\,,\,\}_1,\{\,,\,\}_2)$ of that generic algebraic type admitting a bi-integrable system $\mathcal{F}$ in the above sense, with the functions of $\mathcal{F}$ globally defined on the whole of $M$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in the survey on finite-dimensional integrable systems by Bolsinov, Izosimov and Tsonev. Searches reveal active study of Jordan–Kronecker decompositions of Poisson pencils and bi-Hamiltonian singularities (Bolsinov–Oshemkov, Bolsinov–Izosimov), but no global existence theorem for bi-integrable systems for arbitrary algebraic type. The status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing numbered open problems including bi-integrability and algebraic types of Poisson pencils.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as an open problem in the survey.

status_evidence.title: Singularities of bi-Hamiltonian systems
status_evidence.snippet: Bolsinov–Izosimov study local structure of compatible Poisson pencils via Jordan–Kronecker invariants.
status_evidence.claim: Related work develops the local theory but does not resolve global existence for each algebraic type.

status_evidence.title: Bi-Hamiltonian structures and singularities of integrable systems
status_evidence.snippet: Bolsinov–Oshemkov analyze algebraic types of pencils and their associated integrable systems.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial constructions but not for all algebraic types globally.
